author: blu
body: An integer literal's token text is either decimal digits or a hash followed by hex digits, both with optional grouping underscores. The hash form denotes a raw 64-bit bit pattern, so sixteen f digits mean minus one, which is what a mask author intends. The text-to-integer builtin understands neither the hash form nor grouping underscores, so every consumer of a literal's text calls lit-text-to-integer instead of calling it directly. dec-text-value skips underscores the same way hex-text-value does, so a grouped decimal literal like 1_000_000 yields its plain value rather than a corrupted one.

author: blu
body: A literal PATTERN keeps its source spelling rather than its value, because the text emitter prints that spelling back verbatim and the round-trip has to reproduce the arm the author wrote. IrLitPat also drops the LiteralKind at lowering, so by the time a backend compares a scrutinee against a pattern the only thing left is the text. For every literal kind but one that is harmless: an integer pattern spells digits, and a character pattern was already reduced to digits by the desugarer. A Boolean spells True or False, and running those letters through dec-text-value yields a number no Boolean can equal, so the comparison never fires and the arm can never be taken. Backends compare through here instead. Neither spelling can collide with an integer literal, which is digits or a hash followed by hex.
